name: Electronic Technologies International, Inc.
old_description: At ETI, we’re not simply a contract manufacturer of electronic assemblies, we’re an experienced supply chain partner. Combined with American Cable & Harness (ACH), our customers with complex or challenging projects count on us for rugged, precise and reliable PCB assembly, wire and cable harness assembly and integrated box build solutions.
about:
Electronic Technologies International, Inc. (ETI) operates from Fort Atkinson, Wisconsin, where it was founded in 1958. The company functions as a contract manufacturer of electronic assemblies and a supply chain partner, working in combination with American Cable & Harness (ACH) to serve customers with complex projects.

ETI provides printed circuit board assembly (surface mount, through-hole, and mixed technology), wire and cable harness assembly, and integrated box build solutions. Its capabilities include fine-pitch device placement such as BGAs, micro-BGAs, and LGAs, along with new product introduction (NPI) processes and design-for-manufacturability (DFM) support. Quality inspection uses 3D automated optical inspection, X-ray, and functional testing to IPC-A-610 Class II and III standards. The company states its vertically integrated model has been in place since 1990.

ETI serves medical equipment (respirators, controls for examination tables and dental chairs), aeronautics and aviation (cabin lighting and controls for corporate jets), heavy equipment and machinery (high-density mobile storage systems, gaming systems), HVAC industrial controls (commercial dehumidifiers, heat transfer equipment), industrial control components for food equipment used in restaurants, hospitals, nursing homes, and schools, and agriculture (controls for milking parlors). Case studies reference Spudnik (potato equipment), Bay Tek (gaming), and customers in specialized power supplies and tube & pipe cutting equipment.

The company emphasizes its combined ETI/ACH structure as a single source for PCB assembly, wire harness, and box build, aiming to minimize supply chain complexity. Its NPI process is described as delivering up to 30 percent faster time-to-market versus traditional prototyping, and DFM support targets design risks such as traceability, environmental stresses, and testing requirements. Quick turnaround on quotes and IPC-certified trainers are noted as service commitments.
